question: 5 years ago, the age of a father was 11 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

5 years ago, the father's age was 11 years more than twice his son's age (Difference = 11).

Every year, the father's age increases by 1, while twice the son's age increases by 2.

Thus, the gap between the father's age and twice the son's age decreases by 1 each year.

To reduce this gap from 11 to 0 (where Father = 2 × Son), it will take exactly 11 years.

Since 5 years have already passed from that point, the remaining time = 11 − 5 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

5 years ago, the age of a father was 11 years more than twice his son's age.

**Formula Used:**

If the present age is A, age 't' years ago = A − t, and age after 't' years = A + t.

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 5 Years Ago
 F - 5 = 2(S - 5) + 11
 
 Present Age
 F = 2S + 6
 
 After x Years
 F + x = 2(S + x)
 
 

 + 5 Years

 

 + x Years

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the present age of the father be F and the son be S.

⇒ Father's age 5 years ago = F − 5

⇒ Son's age 5 years ago = S − 5

⇒ According to the problem: F − 5 = 2 × (S − 5) + 11

⇒ F − 5 = 2S − 10 + 11

⇒ F − 5 = 2S + 1

⇒ F − 2S = 6 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ Let after 'x' years, the father's age be twice the son's age.

⇒ Father's age after x years = F + x

⇒ Son's age after x years = S + x

⇒ According to the condition: F + x = 2 × (S + x)

⇒ F + x = 2S + 2x

⇒ x = F − 2S

⇒ From Equation 1, substitute the value of (F − 2S):

⇒ x = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Ages

When solving age-related problems, we assign variables (like x, y) to present ages and form linear equations based on the given past or future conditions.

Time Shifting (Past & Future Ages)

If the present age is P, then the age 'n' years ago is (P − n) and the age 'n' years in the future will be (P + n). The age difference between two individuals always remains constant over time.

Ratio of Ages

When the ratio of ages of two persons is a : b, their ages can be assumed as ax and bx. If their age ratio after 't' years changes to c : d, then (ax + t) ÷ (bx + t) = c ÷ d.
